item.title: Chatbot wars: The Briefing for 30 January 2026
item.description: Meta’s proposed €1.7 billion takeover of Chinese AI startup Manus is part of a strategy to self-preference its own AI chatbot on WhatsApp, complainant Luzia has told Brazilian and EU competition enforcers. The Spanish AI assistant company claims the proposed deal amounts to a killer acquisition and reinforces its complaint, which underpins the ongoing antitrust probes into Meta’s new rules banning...

item.title: New Zealand politicians target private equity roll-ups in competition law overhaul
item.description: New Zealand’s parliament will close a public consultation next week on a bill that would allow the country’s antitrust watchdog to consider the “cumulative effect” of serial acquisitions in deal reviews.

item.title: CAT grants amendment applications in Google lawsuits but declines to rule on SMS debate
item.description: The UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has declined to rule on whether Epic Games can amend its damages claim against Google to cite the Competition and Markets Authority’s recent designation of the company as having strategic market status in its mobile ecosystem.

item.title: FTC orders divestitures over health centre quality concerns
item.description: Sevita Health has agreed to divest 128 residential healthcare facilities to secure Federal Trade Commission approval for its $835 million acquisition of ResCare Community Living.

item.title: FTC targets top law firms over DEI hiring
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission has warned 42 major law firms that their participation in a hiring initiative to promote diversity and inclusion may be anticompetitive.

item.title: GCR Awards 2026: voting now open
item.description: Readers are invited to vote for the cases, law firms, lawyers and economists they believe excelled in 2025.

item.title: DOJ approves lifting device and ice deals
item.description: Columbus McKinnon’s $2.7 billion purchase of lifting chain equipment rival Kito Crosby and Reddy Ice’s $126 million acquisition of packaged ice competitor Arctic Glacier both require divestitures, according to the Department of Justice.

item.title: Rinner: “Crying politics” endangers enforcement
item.description: The US antitrust bar risks undermining the predictability of the merger review process by often attributing enforcement actions to politics, former Department of Justice official Bill Rinner has said.

item.title: Ice breaker: The Tipline for 30 January 2026
item.description: The cold snap and icy conditions in Washington, DC, show no signs of breaking up. Assistant Attorney General Abigail Slater, however, is determined to chisel away the anticompetitive harm created by the merger of bagged ice giants Reddy Ice and Arctic Glacier.
